method: Each issue contains only material that had been published by the last day of its month. Sources carry their own availability dates: news by publication, city records by the date the city posted them, HCD annual report rows by the release of that reporting year, Zillow by the month it published, ACS by its December release, RHNA progress by its August 2026 vintage.

lead.title: Newly appointed Atherton Council member says she’s ready to listen, learn
lead.summary: After numerous years on advisory commissions and a failed council bid, Christine David will be joining the Atherton City Council in December after being appointed earlier this month. Photo by Magali Gauthier. Christine David may be new to the Atherton City Council when she takes office in December, but the longtime resident is no stranger […]

lede: 189 items entered the public record across the nine Bay Area counties in September 2026: 136 housing, 19 development, 6 transportation, 28 civic.
The month's decision was local, in Atherton: Newly appointed Atherton Council member says she’s ready to listen, learn (The Almanac, August 26, 2026).
Of the 101 jurisdictions this dashboard tracks, 100 had a published Zillow index; their median typical home stood at $1.24M in the 2026 index, the most recent available when this issue went out.

sections.title: The month in brief
paragraphs: San Mateo County accounted for the most of the local record, with 44 items. Every county produced something.

sections.title: Still in play
paragraphs: Decisions taken earlier that still set the terms this month.

items.title: SB 79's upzoning provisions take effect
items.snippet: From 1 July, qualifying housing near major transit stops is an allowed use at state-set densities in the counties the law covers, whatever local zoning says, unless a city has adopted a conforming or alternative plan.

items.title: Tracking SB 79 implementation before the train leaves the station
items.snippet: A survey of how cities were preparing for 1 July: conforming ordinances, parcel exclusions, and alternative plans, with MTC publishing a regional map of the transit zones the law reaches.

items.title: Two tax measures, one ballot: San Francisco parcel tax and the regional sales tax move forward
items.snippet: San Francisco voters face a Muni parcel tax alongside the regional sales tax in November, a combination with consequences for how each is campaigned for.

sections.title: Housing and development
paragraphs: Prices first, because they frame everything else. The median typical home across the tracked cities stood at $1.24M in Zillow's 2026 index, 1.2% below the same index a year earlier, with median asking rent at $3,298. That is a regional middle: Atherton at $8.36M and Emeryville at $432,942 are the ends of it.

Counting every record published up to this issue and not reported as finished, 1,792 developments carrying 76,796 reported homes were somewhere between application and construction - 321 review, 1470 approved, 1 construction. That is a count of paperwork, not of homes anyone can move into: a single master plan can carry thousands of units and take a decade.

Against the state's own yardstick, the 35 cities with a published 6th cycle progress row had permitted 22,314 of 171,306 allocated homes, 13.0% of the way through a cycle that runs to 2031. The spread is the story: Morgan Hill at 63.6% and Colma at 0.5%.

Voters in the five SB 63 counties decide the regional transit sales tax - a half cent, a full cent in San Francisco, about $980 million a year for 14 years. It qualified by citizens' initiative in May, so it passes on a simple majority.

notYet: The 2026 state housing annual reports, filed the April after that reporting year.

sections.title: The month in brief
paragraphs: San Mateo County accounted for the most of the local record, with 35 items. Napa, San Francisco produced nothing this dashboard could verify: an absence of published reporting rather than evidence that nothing happened.

sections.title: Still in play

items.title: SB 79's upzoning provisions take effect
items.snippet: From 1 July, qualifying housing near major transit stops is an allowed use at state-set densities in the counties the law covers, whatever local zoning says, unless a city has adopted a conforming or alternative plan.

items.title: Tracking SB 79 implementation before the train leaves the station
items.snippet: A survey of how cities were preparing for 1 July: conforming ordinances, parcel exclusions, and alternative plans, with MTC publishing a regional map of the transit zones the law reaches.

items.title: Two tax measures, one ballot: San Francisco parcel tax and the regional sales tax move forward
items.snippet: San Francisco voters face a Muni parcel tax alongside the regional sales tax in November, a combination with consequences for how each is campaigned for.

sections.title: Housing and development
paragraphs: Prices first, because they frame everything else. The median typical home across the tracked cities stood at $1.24M in Zillow's 2026 index, 1.2% below the same index a year earlier, with median asking rent at $3,298. That is a regional middle: Atherton at $8.36M and Emeryville at $432,942 are the ends of it.

Counting every record published up to this issue and not reported as finished, 1,792 developments carrying 76,796 reported homes were somewhere between application and construction - 321 review, 1470 approved, 1 construction. That is a count of paperwork, not of homes anyone can move into: a single master plan can carry thousands of units and take a decade.

Against the state's own yardstick, the 35 cities with a published 6th cycle progress row had permitted 22,314 of 171,306 allocated homes, 13.0% of the way through a cycle that runs to 2031. The spread is the story: Morgan Hill at 63.6% and Colma at 0.5%.

sections.title: Housing and development
paragraphs: Prices first, because they frame everything else. The median typical home across the tracked cities stood at $1.25M in Zillow's 2025 index, 1.6% below the same index a year earlier, with median asking rent at $3,150. That is a regional middle: Atherton at $7.32M and Rio Vista at $469,080 are the ends of it.

Counting every record published up to this issue and not reported as finished, 1,791 developments carrying 76,795 reported homes were somewhere between application and construction - 320 review, 1470 approved, 1 construction. That is a count of paperwork, not of homes anyone can move into: a single master plan can carry thousands of units and take a decade.

sections.title: The month in brief
paragraphs: 3 decisions above the level of any single city landed in June 2026. BART adopts an FY27 budget with $18 million in cuts (BART, June 11, 2026). Tracking SB 79 implementation before the train leaves the station (Holland & Knight, June 2026). Two tax measures, one ballot: San Francisco parcel tax and the regional sales tax move forward (Greenberg Traurig, June 2026).

California's Department of Housing and Community Development published the 2025 annual progress reports this month: 100 jurisdictions in the nine counties reporting 22,344 homes permitted, 35,919 entitled and 23,776 completed in that reporting year. These are the cities' own submissions, not an independent count, and a permit is not a finished home.
San Mateo County accounted for the most of the local record, with 461 items. Every county produced something.

sections.title: Housing and development
paragraphs: Prices first, because they frame everything else. The median typical home across the tracked cities stood at $1.25M in Zillow's 2025 index, 1.6% below the same index a year earlier, with median asking rent at $3,150. That is a regional middle: Atherton at $7.32M and Rio Vista at $469,080 are the ends of it.

Counting every record published up to this issue and not reported as finished, 1,791 developments carrying 76,795 reported homes were somewhere between application and construction - 320 review, 1470 approved, 1 construction. That is a count of paperwork, not of homes anyone can move into: a single master plan can carry thousands of units and take a decade.

sections.title: What to watch
paragraphs: Dates already on the calendar when this issue went out.

watch.what: Cities file their 2026 housing annual reports with HCD. Table A2 of those filings is what this dashboard's project records are built from, and it reaches data.ca.gov in the months after.

SB 79's upzoning provisions take effect near major transit stops in Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo and Santa Clara counties. Cities can conform, exclude parcels, or adopt an alternative transit-oriented plan before then.

Voters in the five SB 63 counties decide the regional transit sales tax - a half cent, a full cent in San Francisco, about $980 million a year for 14 years. It qualified by citizens' initiative in May, so it passes on a simple majority.
Zillow's 2026 index lands, the next comparable annual reading of home values and rents in these cities.

notYet: The 2026 state housing annual reports, filed the April after that reporting year.
HCD's August 2026 update of the 6th cycle RHNA progress file; allocations adopted in 2021 and 2022 are quoted instead.
Zillow index values from 2026 onward.

sections.title: Housing and development
paragraphs: Prices first, because they frame everything else. The median typical home across the tracked cities stood at $1.25M in Zillow's 2025 index, 1.6% below the same index a year earlier, with median asking rent at $3,150. That is a regional middle: Atherton at $7.32M and Rio Vista at $469,080 are the ends of it.

Counting every record published up to this issue and not reported as finished, 10 developments carrying 8,513 reported homes were somewhere between application and construction - 9 approved, 1 construction. That is a count of paperwork, not of homes anyone can move into: a single master plan can carry thousands of units and take a decade.

SB 79's upzoning provisions take effect near major transit stops in Alameda, Contra Costa, San Francisco, San Mateo and Santa Clara counties. Cities can conform, exclude parcels, or adopt an alternative transit-oriented plan before then.

sections.title: Housing and development
paragraphs: Prices first, because they frame everything else. The median typical home across the tracked cities stood at $1.25M in Zillow's 2025 index, 1.6% below the same index a year earlier, with median asking rent at $3,150. That is a regional middle: Atherton at $7.32M and Rio Vista at $469,080 are the ends of it.

Counting every record published up to this issue and not reported as finished, 8 developments carrying 8,399 reported homes were somewhere between application and construction - 8 approved. That is a count of paperwork, not of homes anyone can move into: a single master plan can carry thousands of units and take a decade.

lead.title: Builder's remedy bill SB 457 fails to advance from the Senate Housing Committee
lead.summary: A measure to narrow how the builder's remedy can be used against cities that miss their housing element deadlines did not clear its first policy committee, leaving the remedy's reach unchanged for Bay Area cities out of compliance.

lede: 10 items entered the public record across the nine Bay Area counties in April 2025: 6 housing, 1 development, 2 transportation.
The month's decision came from Sacramento: Builder's remedy bill SB 457 fails to advance from the Senate Housing Committee (Office of Senator Josh Becker, April 29, 2025).
Of the 101 jurisdictions this dashboard tracks, 100 had a published Zillow index; their median typical home stood at $1.27M in the 2024 index, the most recent available when this issue went out.

sections.title: The month in brief
paragraphs: 1 decision above the level of any single city landed in April 2025. Builder's remedy bill SB 457 fails to advance from the Senate Housing Committee (Office of Senator Josh Becker, April 29, 2025).

San Mateo County accounted for the most of the local record, with 5 items. Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, Solano, Sonoma produced nothing this dashboard could verify: an absence of published reporting rather than evidence that nothing happened.

sections.title: Housing and development
paragraphs: Prices first, because they frame everything else. The median typical home across the tracked cities stood at $1.27M in Zillow's 2024 index, 7.7% above the same index a year earlier, with median asking rent at $3,106. That is a regional middle: Atherton at $7.18M and Rio Vista at $476,177 are the ends of it.

Counting every record published up to this issue and not reported as finished, 3 developments carrying 7,579 reported homes were somewhere between application and construction - 3 approved. That is a count of paperwork, not of homes anyone can move into: a single master plan can carry thousands of units and take a decade.

sections.title: Who decides, and where
paragraphs: Land use in every one of these 101 jurisdictions is decided in public by a planning commission and a city or town council. Agendas are posted before each meeting and public comment is taken at it. Nothing in this newsletter is a decision; anything still pending is decided at one of those meetings.
